feature: ShaneBot Active Cards - invoice/subscription/score/data-answer cards rendered inline in the real artifacts/portal chat shell (/support, support.tsx), driven by card_router + customer_entitlements grounding's cardData (shanebot-engine.ts). Supersedes the #366 manifest's prior assumption of a portal-v2 support-chat.tsx surface - portal-v2 is retired (see CLAUDE.md); this is the real #2519 build against the fresh artifacts/portal scaffolding (#1673).
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the real, deterministic surface of #2519/#366 - that POST /api/msp/support/chat is auth-gated, that a logged-in customer gets a real structured response (content block array), and that the real /support route in artifacts/portal actually mounts (honest sign-in-required state for an unauthenticated visitor, since RequireAuth gates the whole app - see App.tsx).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, AND WHY (card non-determinism): whether a [SHOW_CARD:x] marker (and therefore an actual `{type:'card',...}` block) appears in any given reply is a live-model judgment call (claude-haiku-4-5 deciding, per-turn, whether the user's question warrants a card) - it cannot be forced or seeded, the same class of non-determinism already documented for /api/quiz/submit (MEMORY: quiz-scoring-no-deterministic-endpoint). A UI/API step asserting 'a card renders for this exact prompt' would be flaky by construction, so it is not attempted here. Instead: card_router's parse/gate/strip, the customer_entitlements builder's cardData assembly (invoice/subscription/score/data-answer, real DB rows), and the full propose-resolve-strip flow in the /msp/support/chat handler all have full DETERMINISTIC unit coverage with a mocked model reply: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/shanebot-engine.test.ts and artifacts/api-server/src/routes/support-chat.test.ts.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, AND WHY (no portal login page yet): the rebuilt artifacts/portal (#1673 scaffolding) has NO login page today - App.tsx's RequireAuth renders an honest 'Sign in required' panel for an unauthenticated visitor rather than a redirect to a route that does not exist yet (see App.tsx's own comment). So a real end-to-end UI login -> chat -> reply flow cannot be exercised through the browser right now for ANY portal page, not just this one - this is a structural gap in the portal rebuild, not a defect in the #2519 build. The uiSteps below therefore only assert what is honestly reachable today (the route mounts, RequireAuth's honest empty state renders). The chat surface itself - [data-testid='support-chat-input'], [data-testid='support-chat-send'], [data-testid='support-chat-latest-reply'], [data-testid='support-chat-escalate'] - is real, built, and wired to the real endpoint (support.tsx); once a portal login page exists, extend this manifest's uiSteps with a real login block (matching the pattern other msp-portal manifests use) followed by goto /portal/support and exercising those same selectors - no code change needed on the chat surface side.
ENV VARS (BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables): DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD (the same designated testbed portal account other msp-portal manifests use).
logger channel for the endpoint under test: `engine.shanebot`.
